$comment: Cross-fragment and cross-bottoms-out changes found while QA-ing data/10-silicon.json. None of these were applied: the targets live in files this agent does not own, or under c64.bottoms-out / metal.*, which CHECKLIST section 8 reserves for the maintainer. Nothing here is a rename or an id change.
note: WHAT CHANGED IN 10-silicon.json FIRST, because these proposals only make sense on top of it. The fragment used to inline the whole generic wafer-fab subtree once per chip: ten copies of '100 mm CZ silicon wafer', ten of the polysilicon/SiHCl3/metallurgical-silicon chain, ten fused-quartz crucibles, ten 'CZ pull, saw, lap, polish, clean' steps, nine 'Photolithography for this part' with nine copies of the photoresist and nine spin coaters, eight wafer-cleaning steps, seven chromite-ore nodes, seven gold-bonding-wire nodes. All of that is now ONE shared chain, written once in the fragment's `shared` map with an si.* id and referenced by id from every chip, so the ten chips genuinely converge on one silicon supply line and one packaging line. 351 nodes became 159. The shared nodes are still this fragment's own, because they carry 1982-specific material (4-inch wafers, SiHCl3 from a 98% furnace product, HF consumption per wafer) that the metals fragment does not. Every one of them is a merge candidate, listed below - the point is that there is now exactly ONE of each to merge instead of ten.

merges.why: the electronic-grade polysilicon charge; same substance. Kept here only because this fragment's copy carries the Siemens reactor detail and the 1982 purity caveat that metal.silica.polysilicon also records - reconcile the two purities (9N-11N merchant against 6N-7N in 1982) when folding.
the Siemens wire-heated (UHF) deposition reactor is the same machine as metal.silica.polysilicon.deposition; merge and keep the filament/1150 C detail in the survivor's description.

trichlorosilane, 31.8 C boiling point, distilled to 9-11N. Identical substance and identical boiling-point figure; this fragment's version adds the 250-350 C fluidised-bed make and the 1 ppb boron cut.

metallurgical silicon 98-99%, including the node NAME, which is why audit rule 4 still reports a duplicate. IMPORTANT DISAGREEMENT to resolve on merge: this fragment records B 200-400 ppm / P 100-200 ppm in the furnace output, metal.silica.mgsi records B 5-20 ppm for what it names the same material. One of them is wrong or they describe different points in the chain. The electronics budget (boron below 1 ppb after distillation) is not in dispute.
the three-electrode submerged arc furnace, 1900-2200 C, 200-400 kA, ~11-13 MWh per tonne. Same machine; merge the furnace-size and throughput figures.

the 5-30 mm high-purity quartz lump charged to the silicon furnace is the silicon grade of metal.quartzite (97-99% SiO2). Note that metal.quartzite's own subtree already hangs off metal.silica.submerged-arc-furnace, so merging this removes a second path to the same rock.

the leached sand the lump is crushed from, and the sand the crucibles and the EMC filler are made from. CAREFUL: 15 edges in 30-/35-/40-/60-/70-/90-peripherals resolve their 'quartz sand' ingredient onto THIS node today because its id ends in quartz-sand and this fragment sorts before 60-metals. Merging moves those 15 links onto whatever survives; that is an improvement, but check them.

semiconductor-grade quartz purification (HF/HNO3 leach, Cl2 chlorination at 800-1000 C). No canonical purification node exists in the metals fragment; either keep this one where it is or add a purification node under metal.quartzite.
same node NAME as the metals fragment's, which is the second audit rule 4 duplicate. Same retort, same reaction, same sulfuric-acid route; only the etch duty is silicon-specific.
acid-grade fluorspar concentrate; the metals fragment publishes the canonical node and already reaches it from its own HF branch.
the vein and stock ore the concentrate is floated from. One edge in 70-petrochem currently resolves onto this node.
contact-process sulfuric acid, the feed for the HF retort and the Piranha clean.
elemental sulfur from the Claus process; 80-industry publishes the node.

the low-ash petroleum coke charged to the silicon furnace. metal.silica.petcoke is the silicon grade; metal.coke is the general coke-oven product. Neither carries the delayed-coking/calcining description in si.polysilicon.coke.calciner, so prefer moving that text across with the merge.
halite for the chlor-alkali cell that makes the chlorine and hydrogen behind every gram of trichlorosilane.
HCl gas, dried with concentrated sulfuric acid; 35-logic publishes the same node.

the Czochralski pull. This fragment's version is the 1982 one: 100 mm boule, 1-1.5 m long, boron to 10-20 ohm-cm, helium or argon; metal.silica.czochralski says 0.5-2 mm/min and 75-150 mm. Keep the 1982 numbers when folding.

the fused quartz CZ crucible, flame-fused around a graphite mandrel. metal.silica.czochralski.crucible is thinner and says a few hundred pulls; this fragment's service life of a handful of pulls for a small internal device fab is the more useful figure - reconcile them.

CROSS-FRAGMENT, the other direction: 30-passives has a 'synthetic diamond abrasive' node under its MLCC dicing blade and 30-passives also has its own resin-bonded blade. Three fragments now describe the same belt-press product for the same reason (a diamond-impregnated blade). si.wafer.diamond is the richest of the three; if the maintainer prefers a metals home, metal.silica is the wrong place and a new node is needed. 35-logic had one too (mb.logic.bipolar.wafer.saw.diamond) but it has since deleted it.
chromite (FeCr2O4) concentrate, the ore behind every mask plate's chromium absorber in this tree. The metals fragment owns both the chromium and the chromite nodes.

99.5% sputter-target chromium. Note that this merge also releases the 'chromium' ingredient key, which four nodes in 35-logic and 40-chassis currently resolve onto si.mask.chrome's predecessor mb.cpu.mask.chromium; after the merge they should land on metal.chromium, which is where they belong.

renames.why: ALREADY APPLIED as a data/_aliases.json entry (mb.cpu.wafer -> si.wafer) rather than as a rename, because 35-logic.json started referencing mb.cpu.wafer while this pass was running and the build was failing. The two ids now resolve to the same node. Recorded here so the reviewer can see it was deliberate: the old id is a CPU-scoped path for what is now the shared substrate of all ten chips. Remove the alias once 35-logic points at si.wafer.

ALREADY APPLIED as a data/_aliases.json entry (mb.cpu.wafer.diamond -> si.wafer.diamond) for the same reason - 35-logic references it. Same instruction: remove the alias when the reference is re-pointed.

crossFragmentNotes: I appended two entries to data/_aliases.json (mb.cpu.wafer -> si.wafer, mb.cpu.wafer.diamond -> si.wafer.diamond). That is the only file outside 10-silicon.json and data/_proposals/ that I touched, and it was necessary: 35-logic.json started referencing the two CPU-scoped ids while this pass was in flight, and an agent may still be mid-flight on that file. The build now reports both rewrites, so the change is visible rather than silent. If 35-logic has since moved to si.*, delete both alias lines.

35-logic.json has rebuilt its own copy of the same generic wafer tree (mb.logic.bipolar.wafer.*, mb.logic.bipolar.wafer.polysilicon.hydrogen.*, mb.logic.bipolar.litho.*). After this fragment collapsed to shared si.* nodes, the same duplication now exists twice rather than eleven times: once here and once there. If the two si.* and mb.logic.bipolar.* chains are merged into metal.silica.*, both go at once. I have not touched it.

35-logic.json was the source of two build errors unrelated to this fragment ('mb.logic.cmos.process.wells' and 'mb.logic.cmos.process.locos.phosphoric' both referenced 'mb.logic.bipolar.process.epi.phosphine', which is defined nowhere). They reproduce with the pre-edit 10-silicon.json in place, so they are not mine; they have since been resolved by their owner.

si.emc.silica deliberately keeps 'silica' as the last segment of its id: six edges in 60-metals, 70-petrochem and 80-industry resolve their 'silica filler'/'ground silica' ingredient onto it. If it is ever renamed, those six links fall through to metal.silica-sand via data/_ingredients.json.
si.polysilicon.quartz-sand likewise keeps 'quartz sand' as its id tail for the same reason (15 inbound links).

The metals fragment's metal.silica and metal.silica.polysilicon both assert that 'the 6510 is NMOS, so the 1982 die uses aluminium gate metal and thermally grown field oxide, not a polysilicon gate'. The MOS/CSG 6510 datasheet says 'HMOS, silicon gate, depletion load technology' and this fragment's front-end branch is built on a polysilicon gate. I have followed the datasheet and recorded the disagreement in mb.cpu's note; whoever owns 60-metals should decide which way to correct it.

Not mine, but worth watching centrally: unlinked.catalogue has fallen from the ~377 adopted nodes quoted in the brief to 2 during this pass, and the whole tree from 3590 to 2711. That is the other agents' merges, not deletions - metal.* is still 643 nodes - but the catalogue is the only route to whatever remains published-but-unlinked, so it should be checked at the end.
